surprises.description: The preview said the top of the full-year EPS range was a loss of only $0.25 per share; the company instead guided to a full-year GAAP loss of $1.80–$2.05 per share. That is a substantially worse outlook than the preview’s stated expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: Full-year 2026 guidance calls for GAAP loss per share of $1.80–$2.05.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “On EPS, the top of the FY range (−$0.25) requires roughly +$0.52 of Q4 EPS.”

surprises.description: The preview treated a quantified Catalyst savings target of roughly $15–25 million or more, with timing, as a key expected disclosure. The reported facts describe $13.8 million of SG&A charges, a 230-basis-point gross-margin impact, and restructuring actions, but provide no dollar savings target or timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Project Catalyst restructuring drove $13.8 million of SG&A charges and 230 basis points of gross margin impact,” targeting facility closures, AI efficiencies, software sunsetting, and workforce reductions; no savings target or timing is reported in the facts.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A credible incremental number ($15–25M+, with timing) is the single largest swing factor.”

surprises.description: Active earning coaches fell to about 10,200, below the preview’s 10,300–10,800 base range and representing an estimated 12.8% sequential decline from Q2’s 11,700. The preview identified a decline below 8% sequentially as stabilization, so the coach base contracted faster than that benchmark.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Active earning coaches fell to approximately 10,200 from 19,500 a year earlier,” with management expecting further declines through year-end.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “~10,300–10,800”; the preview said “Deceleration to <8% q/q (~10,800+) means the base is stabilizing.”

surprises.description: Adjusted net loss was $2.1 million, or $0.19 per share, better than the preview’s base expectation of a $0.25–$0.40 adjusted loss per share. The reported adjusted loss also beat the cited $0.35 consensus loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net loss was $2.1 million ($0.19 per share) excluding Catalyst charges.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario projected “EPS (ex-items) $(0.25) – $(0.40)”; the consensus table listed diluted EPS of “$(0.35).”

surprises.description: Revenue per active earning coach reached $7,064, slightly above the preview’s expected range of roughly $6,800–$7,000. The preview expected another increase, but the reported level exceeded its upper estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Average revenue per active earning coach rose 54.1% year-over-year to $7,064,” with coach productivity up an estimated 8% sequentially.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected a fourth increase “to ~$6,800–7,000.”

surprises.description: The preview flagged Trilivy traction as an issue to watch but did not forecast adoption on this scale or the reported retention advantage. By September, 95% of active earning coaches were offering the line, and Premier+ retention from the first to second month was 6 percentage points above Premier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adoption of the new Trilivy Reset product line was rapid, with 95% of active earning coaches offering the line to clients by September, and Premier+ first-to-second-month retention running 6 percentage points higher than Premier.”

surprises.description: The preview expected the full-year revenue range to narrow toward $280–$290 million. The company’s $280–$300 million range raised the lower end from the preview’s $270 million guide arithmetic, but retained a $300 million upper end rather than narrowing to the expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $280–$300 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s guide arithmetic used “FY guidance of $270–300M,” while its base scenario expected the “FY range narrowed toward $280–290M.”

surprises.description: Top coach leaders investing their own capital through ownership stakes was not anticipated in the preview. Management presented the investments as evidence of field confidence in the 3.0 strategy.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A select group of top coach leaders are investing their own capital through ownership stakes in the company,” which management framed as a “generational moment” signaling field confidence in the 3.0 strategy.
